conditions: Same finite binary H and Tanner representation for both premises. Completion feasibility assumes uniform check degree d_c>=2 and sets all coordinates outside the root component to0. Quantitative bound assumes fixed integers3<=d_v<d_c, H (d_v,d_c)-regular, length n>0. No girth or connectedness assumption. Asymptotic statement holds with both degrees fixed.

whole_result: At uniform d_c>=2, choose a root variable, set omega_i=(d_c-1)^(-t) at root-component distance2t and0 elsewhere; omega is nonzero and in K(H). If fixed3<=d_v<d_c and H is regular, then w_AWGN^min(H)<=[d_v(d_v-1)/(d_v-2)]^2 n^beta with beta=log((d_v-1)^2)/log((d_v-1)(d_c-1))<1. Consequently w_AWGN^min(H)/n tends to0 along any such fixed-degree length-growing family. This includes disconnected H and requires no girth hypothesis.
explanation: At a check at distance2t+1, neighbors lie at2t or2t+2. One shallow neighbor is balanced by the other d_c-1 deep weights exactly; two or more shallow neighbors support each maximal weight, and all deep weights are no larger. This also handles d_c=2. Outside the root component all local weights are0. For regular H let m<=n be its root-component size, a=d_v-1,b=d_c-1,r=ab, capacities C0=1,Ct=d_v*b*r^(t-1). BFS nonbacktracking expansion gives Nt<=Ct. Let T first satisfy sum_{0..T}Ct>=m. The mass-m vector filling shallow capacities first has every prefix sum>=the actual layer counts; decreasing weights b^(-t) therefore give ||omega||1<=sum_{0..T}Ct*b^(-t)<=d_v/(d_v-2)*a^T. Root weight gives ||omega||2^2>=1. For T>=1, A_(T-1)<m<=n and A_(T-1)=1+d_v*b/(r-1)*(r^(T-1)-1)>=r^(T-1), so T<=1+log(n)/log(r); T=0 is immediate. W then yields minAWGN<=w(omega)<= [d_v/(d_v-2)]^2*a^(2T)<=B*n^beta. Since b>a, beta<1. Fixed degrees give the stated relative limit.
scope: Whole current C theorem. Does not certify that this vector is globally minimal, Hamming distance/BSC sublinearity, or a scheduling/SPE transfer. Does not extend the rate to d_v=2,d_v>=d_c or variable-degree families.
